findings.why: Same storyline and point: a teenager takes a summer job in an older woman's bakery, rushes and fails at the dough, the terse mentor gives a cryptic answer about knowing when dough is ready ('It tells you' / 'I know what ready looks like'), and the narrator learns readiness can only be noticed, not taught, ending with a small wordless acknowledgment. (The silent-mentor/no-praise/object-handed-over-without-comment beats also echo CLD-P-ACT-R-000017 'Keep It Sharp' and CLD-P-ACT-R-000004 'The Middle Octave', so this bank already has several of these.)
findings.questions_overlap: Partial: both sets ask for a central idea about learning a craft through attention/patience rather than instruction or speed, and both ask how to read the mentor's cryptic line about dough readiness (032 Q8 'It tells you'; 001 Q9 'I know what ready looks like'). Their detail and vocabulary items differ.

findings.why: Both cover urban heat and street trees as shade and cooling infrastructure, but 006 argues about how to fund and measure tree programs (canopy, not trees planted), while 031 explains the causes of the heat island and weighs reflective coatings against trees.
findings.questions_overlap: Minimal: both include an item on trees' slow or long-term payoff (031 Q6; 006 Q2/Q6), but the main-idea and inference items test different claims.

findings.why: The SAT text 'Night heat' makes the same specific point that 031 builds on: urban heat matters most at night because pavement releases stored heat and the body cannot recover. It is a short text, not a full-argument repeat.
findings.questions_overlap: Low: the SAT item tests sentence function. 031 Q5 tests the same 'body can't recover at night' idea, so a student who saw one would have a head start on that one item.

findings.why: Both are humanities essays on a music-history technology as imperfect evidence of performance, and both pivot on a 'None of this means X is useless/worthless as evidence' paragraph. The arguments differ, though: 026 says notated tempo can't anticipate performance conditions, while 029 says the recording medium reshaped how musicians performed.
findings.questions_overlap: Some structural overlap: each has an item on the paragraph that qualifies the critique by affirming the source's evidentiary value (029 Q5; 026 main-claim/final-sentence items). The content tested is different.

findings.why: Both draw on the same real crow-trapping and banding research in which crows come to associate their trappers with danger. 105 concludes that crows recognize individual faces, while 294 hypothesizes that they avoid the place itself.
findings.questions_overlap: No: 105 tests rhetorical synthesis of notes on face recognition, and 294 tests what would weaken a place-association hypothesis.

findings.why: Both rest on the mechanism that volcanic sulfur particles reflect sunlight and cool the planet. 024 (Tambora, 1816) illustrates it, while 298 uses it as the norm that Hunga Tonga contradicts by releasing warming water vapor. The point is different, and the pair is across tests.
findings.questions_overlap: Minimal: 024 Q2 asks why the eruption cooled the climate (sulfur reflection), which is the premise of 298, but 298's item tests only the transition ('Instead,').
